newsitem.title: EGYPT: At least 30 dead in Nile bus crash in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: At least 30 dead in Nile bus crash in Egypt.

text.p: At least 30 people died when a packed public transport bus veered off a bridge in Cairo on Tuesday and toppled onto a bank of the Nile River, partially sinking into the mud, police sources said.
Rescue workers pulled at least 30 mud-covered bodies out of the bus and at least 32 people were injured, Major-General Omar al-Bnaway, in charge of river rescue, told Reuters.
Many victims were believed to have died of suffocation.
Frogmen searched the shallow water for more casualties.
Bnaway said some passengers on the bus, carrying about 70 people, walked away from the accident in Rod al-Farag neighbourhood in northern Cairo.

"I was in a micro-bus behind the bus which crashed," said Arafa Abderrahman. "All of a sudden the bus veered and crossed the divider in the middle of the bridge and went into the other lane, narrowly missing an oncoming taxi. Then it went over."
Rescue workers hauled the overturned bus off the bank with a crane and dug through its mud-filled interior for more bodies.
Public buses are an inexpensive and popular means of transportation for many people in Cairo. The bus was travelling on a route between Giza and Ain Shams in north Cairo.
Buses are usually overcrowded, with people standing in the aisles and some hanging out of the open doors.
Residents say that drivers on the bridge in Rod al-Farag often make shortcuts across parts of its exit and entrance ramps to escape traffic, sometimes veering briefly into oncoming cars.
